item.title: Inflation: Jigawa to increase NYSC members’ allowance — Namadi
item.description: By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse The Jigawa State Government has announced plans to increase the ₦5,000 monthly allowance paid to National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members serving in the state to cushion the effects of rising inflation. Governor Umar Namadi disclosed this while addressing Batch C corps members at the Yakubu Gowon NYSC Orientation Camp in Fanisau, Dutse. Namadi acknowledged the contributions of corps members to community development, saying the government would review their allowance to improve their welfare amid rising living costs. “We are aware of your contributions in our communities. Therefore, we will look into and review your monthly allowance to help you manage the effects of recent inflation,” he said. He commended President Bola Tinubu’s administration for increasing the federal monthly allowance for corps members to ₦77,000, assuring them that Jigawa would also review its payment. “On our part, we will follow the footsteps of the Federal Government to review and increase your monthly state allowance,” he added. The governor also announced a one-off settlement allowance of ₦10,000 for each corps member at the end of the three-week orientation programme to assist them in moving to their primary places of assignment. “We will also give each of you ₦10,000 so that when you are posted to your various primary places of assignment, you will have something in your pocket,” he said. Namadi urged ministries, departments and agencies to make adequate arrangements to receive corps members posted to their offices and ensure a smooth transition from the orientation camp to their places of primary assignment. He further pledged to renovate the orientation camp, construct a new hall and provide a standby generator to improve facilities and ensure a reliable power supply. Describing Jigawa as a peaceful state with hospitable residents, the governor encouraged corps members to integrate into their host communities and contribute meaningfully to local development. He congratulated them on their deployment to the state and wished them a successful service year. item.title: Things to know about late ex-Delta gov Uduaghan
item.description: Former Governor of Delta State, Dr. Emmanuel Uduaghan, is dead. Uduaghan passed away on the morning of Monday, according to a press statement by Toju Uduaghan, on behalf of the family. It partly read, “It is with hearts weighed down by immeasurable grief and profound sorrow that we announce the passing to glory of our beloved Father, Brother, Uncle, and Patriarch, His Excellency, Dr. Chief Emmanuel Eweta Uduaghan, former Governor of Delta State, who departed this world on the morning of 19th October 2026. “His passing has left us devastated. Words can hardly express the depth of our sorrow at the loss of a man who meant so much to our family and whose life and service touched countless others across Delta State and Nigeria.” Things to know about late Uduaghan He was born on 22 October 1954 in Warri North Local Government Area of Delta State. He attended Baptist Primary School, Mosogar, between 1961 and 1966; Federal Government College, Warri, between 1968 and 1974; and the University of Benin between 1975 and 1980, earning a Bachelor of Medicine and Surgery (MBBS) degree and a Diploma in Anaesthesia. He was posted to Kwara State for the mandatory one-year National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) in 1981. Between 1989 and 1994, late Uduaghan served in a number of healthcare facilities, such as Shell Clinic Ogunu, Westend Hospital Warri and Benoni Clinic Benin City, Edo State. On return to democracy in 1999, he was appointed as commissioner for health in Delta state. In 2003, Uduaghan was appointed Secretary to the Delta State Government. In 2007, he was elected as governor of Delta State and subsequently re-elected in 2011. On 29 August 2018, he officially announced he had left PDP for APC and returned to the party in 2020. item.title: FG Reaffirms Commitment To Human Capital Development For Economic Growth
item.description: The Federal Government has reaffirmed its commitment to human capital development as a central pillar for economic growth, saying long-term investments in health, education, skills and livelihoods are critical to transforming Nigeria’s economy. The reaffirmation was made during a media engagement in Abuja on Monday organised to keep journalists abreast of developments under the Human Capital Development Programme (HCD) 2.0 and deepen public understanding of its role in national development. National Coordinator of the Human Capital Development 2.0 Programme, Rukayya El-Rufai, said Nigeria’s economic future depends on deliberate and sustained investment in its people. “Nigeria’s future depends on its people. If we do not invest in them, we cannot grow our economy. There’s a lot of investment going into infrastructure, but if you do not invest in human capital, you are not simply going to be able to grow your economy as much,” he said. El-Rufai explained that HCD 2.0 builds on the earlier version introduced under former Vice President Yemi Osinbajo, which focused on health, education and labour force participation. According to her, the new iteration expands the scope to include skills development and livelihoods, to address poverty, underemployment and learning poverty. item.title: Alleged Rights Violation: Court dismisses El-Rufai’s N120m suit
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri, Abuja A High Court of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) sitting at Maitama, Abuja, on Monday dismissed a fundamental rights enforcement suit brought before it by the detained former governor of Kaduna State, Nasir El-Rufai. Listed as respondents in the legal action were the Department of State Services (DSS), the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC), the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), and the Attorney General of the Federation (AGF). El-Rufai, who served as governor from 2015 to 2023 and as minister of the FCT under former President Olusegun Obasanjo’s administration, had accused the respondents in the suit of violating his rights. He further urged the court to invalidate letters of invitation extended to him by both the ICPC and the EFCC and demanded N120 million in damages from the respondents. Delivering judgment in the matter, Justice Sylvanus Oriji held that the legal action was without merit and dismissed it. The court held that the letters of invitation, which requested the former governor to appear before the federal agencies investigating allegations against him, met constitutional requirements and did not infringe his fundamental rights. The court held that the agencies acted within their mandates by inviting him to shed light on issues raised against him. Besides, the court declined to declare that the DSS’s attempt to arrest the applicant at Nnamdi Azikiwe Airport amounted to a violation of his rights. It held that the DSS has a statutory responsibility to maintain a watchlist and to arrest persons of interest. item.title: CAS verdict on Senegal AFCON title appeal ‘expected end November’
item.description: The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) announced Monday that a verdict on Senegal’s appeal of the decision to strip them of the Africa Cup of Nations title in favour of Morocco is expected at the end of November. CAS said in a statement that a hearing of the case took place behind closed doors at its headquarters in Lausanne on October 8. “The panel have begun and continue their deliberations,” the organisation which resolves international sports disputes explained. “The CAS arbitrators have decided to issue a complete ruling which includes legal grounds, known as a CAS Award. This process will require several weeks, with the CAS Award expected at the end of November 2026.” At the January 18 final in Rabat, Senegal won 1-0 thanks to Pape Gueye’s extra-time goal, but the occasion was marred by chaotic scenes near the end of normal time when many Senegal players walked off the pitch in protest at the decision to award Morocco a penalty with the match still goalless. Some Senegalese supporters also attempted a pitch invasion, and the game was held up for almost 20 minutes before the Senegal players returned. In March, the Confederation of African Football (CAF) overturned that result, awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory, and the title. item.title: Flood kills two, submerges 18 communities in Nasarawa
item.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia The Nasarawa State Government has urged residents of flood-prone communities to heed evacuation warnings and move to higher ground following flooding that submerged 18 communities in the Doma Local Government Area, killing two people and displacing several others. The Commissioner for Information, Culture and Tourism, Dr Nawani Aboki, made the appeal on Monday while briefing journalists in Lafia on the impact of the disaster in the affected communities. Aboki said Governor Abdullahi Sule had directed the Director-General of the Nasarawa State Emergency Management Agency to visit the affected communities to assess the damage and determine the necessary interventions. He said the government was working towards providing assistance to residents affected by the disaster. “We are hoping that anytime this week concrete actions will be taken by government. Yesterday, when I was returning, I was there with the chairman of the local government to sympathise with the people and condole with them,” the commissioner said. According to him, two people have died as a result of the flooding, while several others have been displaced. Buildings and farmlands were also reportedly destroyed. Describing the incident as massive flooding, Aboki said residents had been advised against returning to their homes until the floodwaters receded. “It is not just normal flooding, but massive flooding that took place. We are hoping that the flooding will end and the waters dry up so that people can resume their normal activities,” he said. “But we have asked them not to go back yet. Let them wait until we see the water actually receding back to the River Benue. We are not sure if more water will be coming in from the Lagdo Dam in Cameroon; it will even be worse than it is currently,” he added. The commissioner said the government was also prepared to provide support and relief supplies to affected residents to reduce the risk of disease outbreaks following the flooding. He explained that several smaller communities were clustered within larger settlements, complicating efforts to assess the full extent of the damage and the number of people affected. Aboki cited Agyma, where more than eight communities were reportedly affected, and Rukubi and Akpanaja, where several communities were also said to be experiencing the impact of the flooding. The government urged residents in vulnerable areas to prioritise their safety and remain in safer locations until the floodwaters had sufficiently receded. item.description: By Elizabeth Osayande Media Rights Agenda (MRA) has called on the Federal Government to implement a court order directing it to investigate the assassination of renowned journalist and founding Editor-in-Chief of Newswatch magazine, Dele Giwa, and prosecute those found responsible. The call came on Monday, October 19, 2026, as Nigeria marked the 40th anniversary of Giwa’s death. He was killed on October 19, 1986, by a parcel bomb delivered to his residence in Ikeja, Lagos. AFP reporters heard air alerts and explosions ringing out in the capital. “Another Russian ballistic missile attack came in several waves overnight, and once again, there was no early warning from our partners,” Zelensky said on social media. item.description: A Mombasa court will deliver a long-awaited verdict on Monday in the trial of a self-proclaimed Kenyan preacher and his associates, accused of murdering 191 people, mostly children, in an infamous starvation cult. Self-proclaimed pastor Paul Mackenzie is alleged to have incited his acolytes to starve to death in order to “meet Jesus”. In the three years since the grisly discovery, more bodies of children, women and men have been unearthed, bringing the total to well over 400. Mackenzie looked impassive as he arrived at Mombasa Law Courts on Monday with 29 other accused, who descended from a barred-window bus hand-cuffed in pairs. Relatives of the victims were also in court, many making their way to Mombasa from rural communities along the coast. item.title: Semenyo ruled out for eight weeks as Man City sweat over Haaland
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Antoine Semenyo is expected to miss around eight weeks with a knee injury, while Erling Haaland remains a doubt for Manchester City’s Champions League match against AEK Athens on Tuesday. According to Sky Sports, City manager Enzo Maresca said scans showed Semenyo’s injury was less severe than the club had feared. The forward was hurt during Saturday’s 3-2 win over Ipswich Town. “Now the most important thing is for him to recover,” Maresca said. “When he is back in December, it will be like a new player.” Haaland also limped off after the Ipswich match, but Maresca said he could still be available for Tuesday’s game. The striker felt better on Monday, though City were waiting to assess him in training. “We have some doubts after Saturday’s game,” Maresca said. “He was quite good yesterday, better, so we’ll see today.” Mateo Kovacic, Nico O’Reilly and Matheus Nunes also had injury concerns during the Ipswich match. Maresca said the other players were “more or less all okay”, with Semenyo the only player expected to be out for an extended period. City have three points from their first two Champions League matches as Maresca said the team would aim to beat AEK with its best available players after losing its previous game to Paris Saint-Germain. She said, “Words are painfully inadequate to express the depth of my sorrow at the passing of His Excellency, Dr Chief Emmanuel Eweta Uduaghan. item.title: NGX Group named Africa’s Best Exchange at Euromoney Markets Awards 2026

Presented at the Mandarin Oriental Hyde Park, London, on Thursday, 15 October 2026, the award recognises achievements in market development during 2025 and comes amid robust growth in Nigeria’s equities market. A key driver of wider primary-market participation has been NGX Invest, the Group’s electronic public-offering platform, which simplifies subscriptions to public offers and rights issues. The platform played a significant role in Nigeria’s banking sector recapitalisation exercise, facilitating more than ₦2.8 trillion in capital raising. By September 2026, its distribution network had grown to more than 180 channels spanning stockbrokers, banks and fintechs, with a WhatsApp subscription channel providing investors with an additional channel for subscribing to public offers. item.title: Don’t distract Oyebanji with 2030 politics, Tinubu warns

God will help you to perform better.” In his remarks, Oyebanji thanked the people of Ekiti for their support and promised that his second term would deliver greater benefits, with emphasis on industrialisation and shared prosperity. “Let me assure you that my second term will be better than the first term with emphasis on industrialisation and prosperity for our people. In our first, we had put infrastructures in place to attract investors to this state. With industrialisation, employment will be here and everyone will prosper,” the governor said. He, however, stressed that attracting industries would require cooperation between the government, traditional rulers and communities, particularly on land acquisition for investors. “But government alone can’t do it, so we are partnering with our traditional rulers on the issue of land. In his homily, the Bishop of Ekiti Diocese, Anglican Communion, Rt. Rev. Andrew Olusola Ajayi, urged the governor to regard his position as a trust to be exercised in the interest of the people. The cleric said Oyebanji’s second term should be devoted to serving God and humanity, warning that public office carried a responsibility for which he would ultimately be accountable. “Do you know what God wants from you in this second term, it is for you to serve Him and humanity. You are not the owner of Ekiti State, but a steward,” Ajayi said. He urged the governor to maintain his integrity and sustain the qualities that had earned him public trust. “People are talking good things about you. Please, continue in this goodness. You should also maintain your integrity. You are a man of integrity, you must know this,” he said. The First Lady, Prof. Olayemi Oyebanji, led choristers in a special rendition during the service. Dignitaries at the event included former governors Niyi Adebayo, Ayodele Fayose and Segun Oni; former Governor Kayode Fayemi, represented by his wife, Erelu Bisi Fayemi; Senators Yemi Adaramodu and Cyril Fasuyi; and members of the House of Representatives, Femi Bamisile, Sola Fatoba and Biodun Omoleye. Traditional rulers, religious leaders, labour leaders, traders and civil servants were also present. The Bank reported that federal interest payments reached ₦7.7 trillion in the first half of 2026, equivalent to 124 per cent of reported federal revenue. Finance Minister Taiwo Oyedele argues that the comparison is misleading because the interest figure includes obligations serviced on behalf of states, while the revenue figure excludes certain government income. The ministry acknowledges the underlying figures but emphasises that: Federal revenue increased 72 per cent, from ₦3.6 trillion to ₦6.2 trillion. Interest payments increased 38 per cent, from ₦5.6 trillion to ₦7.7 trillion. The reported interest-to-revenue ratio declined from 156 per cent to 124 per cent. The government also cites a World Bank projection putting full-year 2026 debt service at 46 per cent of revenue. These measures use different periods and definitions and should not be treated as directly interchangeable. Why it matters : The disagreement concerns how Nigeria’s fiscal position should be measured, not simply whether public debt is increasing. Business and strategic implications : Investors need consistent fiscal reporting to assess sovereign risk. Whatever the accounting interpretation, substantial interest costs continue to constrain resources available for infrastructure and public services. What to watch : Further World Bank clarification, full-year fiscal accounts, the 2027 budget and whether borrowing costs decline as economic conditions stabilise. 3. State Police: Governors Prepare Security Outfits But Constitutional Approval Lags Police officers undergoing training What happened : An investigation published by Daily Sun on Monday, 19 October, reports that several state governments are recruiting personnel, strengthening vigilance organisations and preparing administrative structures for possible state police services. The constitutional amendment remains unfinished. As of 15 October, only five state assemblies—Edo, Osun, Oyo, Rivers and Zamfara—had approved the proposed amendment, against the 24 approvals required. Meanwhile, the Presidency says a separate National Policing Bill is approximately 90 per cent ready for submission to the National Assembly. Kaduna, Plateau, Imo, Benue and other states have undertaken varying levels of preparation. These measures do not mean that state police forces have been legally established. Why it matters : Nigeria is approaching a potentially fundamental restructuring of its security architecture. Political and strategic implications: Decentralised policing could improve responses to local security threats. However, safeguards against political interference, especially during elections, will be essential. What to watch: Further state assembly approvals, publication of the National Policing Bill, funding arrangements and provisions guaranteeing professional independence. 4. Photo by JOSPIN MWISHA / AFP What happened : Health authorities in the Democratic Republic of Congo confirmed on Sunday, 18 October, that Ebola has spread to North Ubangi, the eighth province affected by the country’s continuing epidemic. Two cases, including one death, have been confirmed in the province, which borders the Central African Republic. According to the latest national situation report, covering the period to 16 October: Total confirmed cases : 9,415. Total deaths : 4,536. New infections in 24 hour s: 67. New deaths : 26. Seven infections have also been confirmed in Kenya this month, while Uganda has previously reported cases. Why it matters : This is now Congo’s worst recorded Ebola outbreak. Its geographical expansion increases the difficulty of containment. African and business implications : Further cross-border transmission could disrupt travel, trade and regional economic activity. There are also substantial risks for healthcare systems and humanitarian operations. What to watch : Cases near international borders, emergency financing, contact tracing and whether infection rates begin declining in the worst-affected provinces. 5. Japan’s Nikkei declined approximately 0.7 per cent in early trading, following a 5.4 per cent fall last week. The final US policy position remains unsettled. China also reported third-quarter economic growth of 4.5 per cent, slightly exceeding market expectations. Its industrial output increased 5.5 per cent in September, although weak domestic demand and property-market difficulties remain concerns. The chairman urged both warring parties to embrace peace and avoid actions capable of escalating tensions. He also called on youths in Paikon-Kore to exercise restraint and promote peaceful coexistence with other residents, warning against confrontation and retaliatory attacks. Ikwa advised farmers whose crops were damaged by cattle to report such incidents to the relevant security agencies rather than resorting to self-help. He noted that such conflicts often affected innocent people who might not even understand the circumstances that triggered the dispute. The chairman further urged residents to cooperate with security personnel deployed to the community, adding that an expanded security meeting had been convened, with youth leaders, the Sarkin Noma and other community leaders from both sides invited to seek a lasting solution. He said anyone who felt unfairly treated or believed their complaints had not received adequate attention should report directly to him for intervention, stressing that grievances must be addressed through lawful channels. The chairman, at the end of the security meeting, set up a peace and investigative committee. He also carried out on-the-spot assessments of the three affected communities that witnessed cases of farmers and herders clashes. Ikwa promised that the committee’s report would be made public during the stakeholders meeting on Monday (today). Some residents, who spoke to our reporter, said the August 11 incident was a result of cows that allegedly strayed into a farm. They claimed that the tension heightened when the owner of the farm confronted the herders for allowing cows to graze inside his farm, a situation which they said led to a serious confrontation that left four persons injured. Ishaku Danjuma, a farmer, explained that a similar incident also happened in Paiko community on the same day, after some cows allegedly grazed inside a maize farm, resulting in clashes between farmers and herders in the community. He said the farmer queried the herders for allowing cows into the farm, which led to the clash. “If you make your investigations, you will discover that 95 per cent of incidents of farmers and herders clashes across the three communities were as a result of cows straying into people’s farms,” he said. A member of the Paiko community, Usman Yakubu, also said the incessant cases of farmers-herders clash were as a result of cows that allegedly invade farms to destroy crops in the rural communities in the area. He alleged that some herders allowed their cows to eat up some crops, a development he said led to serious confrontations between the affected farmers and the herders across the three communities. “It was as a result of the destruction of some crops which suddenly resulted in a confrontation between the affected farmers and herders, which later led to the injuring of four farmers across three villages,” he said.
